continuation_review.topic: Committed cursor and generic legal bindings
continuation_review.conclusion: The lethal branch retains its already committed cursor and sets the existing repeat flag beside its frame-owned receipt. The typed validator accepts the LuochongResolve operation with the descriptor-required Owner target and a legal zero-discard loseHp receipt. It does not hardcode ol:luochong, native trigger ids, instruction index one, current target HP, liveness, or mutable eligibility. Other legal bindings and preceding instructions retain the generic mechanism.

The executor still drains post-instruction windows first, validates gameplay hash and owner/skill eligibility, resets the repeat flag only on active parent resumption, then commits the repeated instruction. The descriptor uses ParseOwnerAlways, so a pending receipt is not skipped by an instruction condition. Luochong's existing winner/skill qualification still runs before pending finalization; no new dispatch or bypass was introduced. The real dying return validates its parent and enters the same runtime program method.

continuation_review.topic: One HP payment and one ledger publication
continuation_review.conclusion: The HP payment occurs only while accepting the original lethal option. Re-entry observes LuochongPending and finalizes without LoseHp. Finalization clears the receipt and repeat flag before publishing the resolution fact and advancing. Round option/target availability remains derived from committed facts; nested windows cannot republish the same pending receipt.

Compared current TengFangLan source against luochong-before.zip. Product changes are limited to decline identity metadata, replacing the lethal rewind with the repeat flag, clearing that flag at finalization, the typed validator and corresponding explanatory comments. Existing accumulated discard behavior remains, and the Luochong resolution event's card collection is already covered by committed event freezing.

new_fixture_review: Seed 31 and a small fixed Dodge deck; every actual selected general's HP, max HP, identity and skill set are asserted after setup. The Lord base HP is three and classic Lord adjustment makes four; peers have four.

The real gameStarting selectTarget and loseHp amount three lower target seat zero or one from four to one. All operations use serialized Submit commands. Reflection only registers existing native content; there is no runtime state, HP, frame or grant injection and no seed search.

The native preparation Luochong binding is asserted to be its first and only instruction. Picking lethal loss must leave the exact committed parent, one HP-loss fact, no ledger fact yet and a real ProgramSkill DyingFrame.
Self-target enters the native Aichen dying-entry child before rescue, cold-restores there and removes one option. The other-target case must produce no Aichen removal.

Both cases use the owner's actual hand Dodge converted to Peach by the fixture's declared response conversion. Cold restoration occurs before paying rescue; the test asserts one HP loss, one surviving dying resolution, one actual rescue response and one Hand-to-Processing payment.

Final ledger and parent binding resolve once; parent, dying frame and pending receipt disappear. A later real native after-damage trigger in the same round excludes the already paid loseHp option and target, then declines and retires its own frame without duplicating the earlier fact.

Cold helper compares every safe player view, exact suspended frames, event envelope identity and payload bytes, physical movement ledger, accepted commands and card-zone diagnostics through a serialized checkpoint prefix. Existing one/two-card discard and immutable pending/event collection checks remain intact.
